nodes.title: SG-1.2 Write pure grid-to-pixels and sprite-sheet functions
nodes.body:
Context: SG-1.1 is done (game/frontend/src/lib/palette.ts exports PALETTE, 48 colours or fewer). The last check found that neither gridToRgba nor buildSpriteSheet exists in any source or test file under game/, although earlier artefacts report 16 passing tests. Desired behaviour: pure functions convert a palette-indexed grid to RGBA and lay frames out into one sheet, with unit tests for width, height, frame count, palette-only colours and out-of-range index rejection. Why: SG-1.3 (PNG script and manifest update) needs these functions.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a palette-indexed grid, when gridToRgba runs, then the result has the grid's width and height and every pixel colour is in the shared palette
- Given a grid containing an index outside the palette range, when gridToRgba runs, then it throws
- Given N equal-size frames, when buildSpriteSheet runs, then the sheet reports frameCount N and width equal to N times the frame width
- Given the same input twice, when either function runs, then the output bytes are identical


## Scope
- In scope: game/frontend/src/lib/gridToRgba.ts
- In scope: game/frontend/src/lib/spriteSheet.ts
- In scope: unit tests under game/frontend/tests
- Out of scope: PNG generation script
- Out of scope: asset manifest update
- Out of scope: sprite source grids
- Out of scope: new rooms, story content, backend, audio, deployment, repository clean-up
- Preserve: game/frontend/src/lib/palette.ts exports
- Preserve: 480x270 constants in game/frontend/src/phaser/config.ts
- Preserve: Phaser ~3.90.0 pin and its guard tests


## Technical constraints
- Phaser stays on 3.90.x; React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, Radix and Zustand stay
- Functions are pure and deterministic; no downloaded art, image services or CDN links
- One shared palette of at most 48 colours, defined once in palette.ts
- Tests are unit tests with all dependencies mocked
- Earlier unmerged work and .devion/worktrees are not read or copied


## Dependencies
- SG-1.1 palette module (done)


## Definition of done
- Both functions exist, are exported and typecheck
- Unit tests import them and pass


## Non-functional requirements
- Output is byte-identical on repeated runs


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · gridToRgba converts a palette-indexed grid to RGBA and rejects out-of-range indices
nodes.body:
Context: no gridToRgba exists under game/. Desired behaviour: gridToRgba(grid, palette = PALETTE) takes rows of palette indices and returns {width, height, data} where data is a Uint8ClampedArray of length width*height*4 with alpha 255. Expected result: every pixel RGB equals a palette colour; any index that is not an integer in 0..palette.length-1, or a ragged row, throws. Why: art is authored as palette-indexed grids.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a 3x2 grid of valid indices, when gridToRgba runs, then width is 3, height is 2 and data length is 24
- Given a valid grid, when each pixel is read back, then its RGB equals the hex colour of the palette entry at that index with alpha 255
- Given an index equal to palette.length, a negative index or a non-integer, when gridToRgba runs, then it throws an Error naming the index
- Given rows of unequal length or an empty grid, when gridToRgba runs, then it throws


## Scope
- In scope: gridToRgba function and RgbaImage type
- Out of scope: transparency
- Out of scope: PNG encoding
- Preserve: PALETTE export


## Technical constraints
- Pure function; reads colours only from the shared palette passed in (default PALETTE from game/frontend/src/lib/palette.ts)
- Palette of at most 48 colours defined once


## Definition of done
- gridToRgba exported from game/frontend/src/lib/gridToRgba.ts


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · buildSpriteSheet lays equal-size frames into one horizontal sheet with size and frame metadata
nodes.body:
Context: no buildSpriteSheet exists under game/. Desired behaviour: buildSpriteSheet(frames) takes RGBA frames {width,height,data} of identical size and returns {width, height, frameWidth, frameHeight, frameCount, data} with frames placed left to right. Expected result: width = frameWidth*frameCount, height = frameHeight, pixels copied unchanged so palette colours are preserved. Empty input or mismatched frame sizes throw. Why: sprite sheets feed the PNG script and manifest in SG-1.3.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given 4 frames of 32x48, when buildSpriteSheet runs, then width is 128, height is 48, frameWidth is 32, frameHeight is 48 and frameCount is 4
- Given frames with distinct pixels, when the sheet is read, then frame i occupies columns i*frameWidth to (i+1)*frameWidth-1 with unchanged pixel values
- Given frames of different sizes or an empty list, when buildSpriteSheet runs, then it throws
- Given sheets built from gridToRgba frames, when every sheet pixel is read, then its colour is in the shared palette


## Scope
- In scope: buildSpriteSheet function and SpriteSheet type
- Out of scope: multi-row layouts
- Out of scope: PNG encoding
- Out of scope: manifest writing
- Preserve: gridToRgba behaviour


## Technical constraints
- Pure function; input frames are not mutated
- Deterministic byte output


## Definition of done
- buildSpriteSheet exported from game/frontend/src/lib/spriteSheet.ts


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: Act: Create gridToRgba in the frontend lib
nodes.body:
Create the pure function that converts a palette-indexed grid to RGBA using PALETTE from palette.ts, throwing on invalid indices or ragged rows.

## Acceptance criteria
- gridToRgba(grid) returns width, height and RGBA data of length width*height*4
- An out-of-range or non-integer index throws


## Scope
- In scope: new file game/frontend/src/lib/gridToRgba.ts
- Out of scope: tests
- Out of scope: spriteSheet
- Preserve: palette.ts unchanged


## Technical constraints
- Shared palette of at most 48 colours is the only colour source
- Pure, deterministic, no I/O
- New file: `game/frontend/src/lib/gridToRgba.ts`


## Definition of done
- File exists, exports gridToRgba and RgbaImage, and tsc --noEmit accepts it


## Clarifying questions
- None

steps.action: Create the file and export interface RgbaImage with fields width: number, height: number and data: Uint8ClampedArray.
steps.code:
import { PALETTE } from './palette';

export interface RgbaImage { width: number; height: number; data: Uint8ClampedArray; }
steps.expected: RgbaImage type is exported from the new file

steps.action: Export gridToRgba(grid: readonly (readonly number[])[], palette: readonly string[] = PALETTE): RgbaImage. Throw if grid is empty, if grid[0] is empty or any row length differs from grid[0].length. For each cell throw an Error naming the index when it is not an integer in 0..palette.length-1. Parse the palette hex into r,g,b with parseInt on slices 1-3, 3-5, 5-7 and write r,g,b,255 at offset (y*width+x)*4.
steps.expected: Valid grids give RGBA data; invalid indices throw

steps.action: Create the file exporting interface SpriteFrame {width:number;height:number;data:Uint8ClampedArray} and interface SpriteSheet extends SpriteFrame with frameWidth, frameHeight and frameCount numbers.
steps.code:
export interface SpriteFrame { width: number; height: number; data: Uint8ClampedArray; }
export interface SpriteSheet extends SpriteFrame { frameWidth: number; frameHeight: number; frameCount: number; }

steps.action: Export buildSpriteSheet(frames: readonly SpriteFrame[]): SpriteSheet. Throw when frames is empty or any frame width/height differs from frames[0]. Allocate data of size frameWidth*frameCount*frameHeight*4 and, for each frame i and row y, copy frame.data.subarray(y*fw*4,(y+1)*fw*4) to offset (y*sheetWidth + i*fw)*4 using data.set.
steps.expected: Frames are laid out left to right with metadata
